## Next implementation contract: canonical quantum Unit maps — 2026-10-05

Under the existing Unit meaning and QS/PR/RS plus EXACT interpretations, select the explicit sealed source entries `std::quantum::unit` and `std::quantum::finish` for the common selected-source hierarchy path. This is an ordinary source/API decision, not a new constitutional interpretation or guarantee. `unit(())` takes exactly one ordinary Unit argument and returns one fresh Q<Unit> owner; `finish(q)` consumes exactly one Q<Unit> owner and returns ordinary Unit. Both have zero static parameters and Unitary quantum action. Their exact coefficients are +1, with no wire, observation, discard, state promise or implicit conversion. Unit, Bit and Bits<0> remain distinct. The explicit argument is evaluated fully exactly once, including its effects and scalar work.

Lower to the existing checked hierarchy pack_unit/unpack_unit constructors and independently validate the source events and frames. Preserve scalar multiplication: finish(phase_eighth(unit(()))) contributes omega, not +1, and four eighth phases under coherent control produce Z. Both round trips, including arbitrary retained reference frames, must preserve their stated exact action. Ordinary owner-product wrappers can implement the explicit left/right interface maps while retaining owner order; these are not packaged-tree Q<(Unit,A)> unitors. General quantum product projection/coherent lifts and packaged-tree unitors remain required subsequent work.

The selected hierarchy profile can support these existing exact constructors; the finite Raw route has no pure owner-introduction/elimination constructor and must give its honest unsupported result. Do not replace finish with observing discard, silently fall back after native failure, or claim that this partial integration completes the common-language migration. Current finite/Raw parity remains required by #32; no scope is deferred or closed here.

Before implementation preserve complete first sources, context, independent equations and actual current-CLI diagnostics under authoring_sessions/quantum-unit-maps-v030. Include introduction/elimination and both round trips, phase/controlled-phase/reference checks, distinct left/right owner-product wrappers, caller argument evaluation, Bit/Bits0/ordinary substitution, arity/static-arity, duplicate/revived/lost owner and effect violations, and packed-product desired sources exposing the next unsupported boundary. Use at most two system qubits. Reuse one bounded build target, retain actual failures and named repairs, then validate both supported Rust toolchains and current native checking. No new native semantic rule or general source-preservation theorem is implied.
